Clairin Ti Punch

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 1Prep 5 min

Clairin Ti Punch is a traditional Haitian cocktail made with clairin, a locally distilled sugarcane spirit, lime, and sugar. It is commonly served during Fete de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa, to honor the spirit of agriculture and the harvest season with a refreshing and potent drink.

Ingredients

  • 2 oz (60 ml) clairin
  • 1/2 lime, cut into wedges
  • 1 tsp (5 ml) raw cane sugar or simple syrup
  • Ice cubes

Method

  1. Place the lime wedges in a small glass.
  2. Add the sugar or simple syrup on top of the lime wedges.
  3. Gently muddle the lime and sugar together to release the lime juice and dissolve the sugar.
  4. Fill the glass with ice cubes.
  5. Pour the clairin over the ice and stir well to combine.
  6. Serve immediately and enjoy responsibly.

Tips

  • Use fresh lime for the best flavor and a traditional taste.
  • Adjust the sugar amount to your preference for sweetness.
  • If clairin is unavailable, substitute with a high-quality white rum for a similar but less authentic experience.
